scope: R6 readiness work: the narrow layout (FE01), the plans/watches panel, the saved-document viewer, and the two decisions docs/92 names

measured.narrow_viewport: 390x844 in headless Chrome against the served React build: main 390px, composer 358px, composer textarea 263px, skip link absolute, document scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth 390 (no horizontal overflow)
measured.drawer: aria-expanded true and data-open true after the topbar Menu control, scrim present, and a surface pick leaves the rail closed
measured.wide_table_on_a_narrow_screen: the warnings table is 539px inside a 390px viewport and scrolls inside its focusable region instead of pushing the page sideways

defect_found_and_fixed: appending to frontend/src/styles/app.css by reading only the first lines truncated the file: the design-system vocabulary (.skip-link, .card, .btn, .reading, .display and the rest) was deleted and the page still rendered, with the skip link in flow taking 175px of the narrow row. Restored from git, re-applied whole, and src/styles/styles.test.ts now names the vocabulary and fails if one is missing.
service_worker_decision: NOT ported in this batch. The plans panel states that a push subscription registers /sw.js and that the subscription is refused while the React build serves no worker. Together with py_vapid not being installed on this machine, browser push is unverified on the React path; the panel never claims delivery.
push_on_this_machine: GET /api/push/vapid-key raises because py_vapid is absent (requirements.txt lists pywebpush==2.5.0, not installed here). The panel shows the route own refusal rather than a control that would fail silently.

default_surface_browser_run.what: the workspace started with no frontend argument, opened in headless Chrome over loopback
